title: Greetings from an isolated region in northern Pakistan's Hindu Kush mountains
first_paragraph: Chitral borders Afghanistan and isn't easy to reach. Breathtaking views abound in this remote mountainous region — as do rockslides and avalanches.

title: U.S. and Iran resume attacks. And, Fauci to face Senate questions on COVID pandemic
first_paragraph: The U.S. and Iran have resumed fighting after Iran attacked U.S. forces in the Middle East yesterday. And, a Senate committee will question Anthony Fauci about the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: New York school pauses plan to deploy humanlike AI robot teacher after backlash
first_paragraph: A school district in upstate New York is pausing plans to deploy an AI-powered, humanoid robot in the classroom after state education officials, teachers and local residents raised concerns.

title: Iran resumes missile attacks as U.S. and Saudis strike Tehran-backed militias in Iraq
first_paragraph: The flare-up on multiple fronts raised the risk of a return to all-out war, underscoring the difficulty of winding down a five-month conflict that has jolted the world economy.

title: 'Machines are collaborators' at this new museum of AI art
first_paragraph: "What is beyond reality?" asks artist Refik Anadol. His latest projects include Dataland, an immersive AI art museum in Los Angeles, and an installation at the Smithsonian in Washington, D.C.

title: As extreme heat grips the South and West, here's how to stay safe
first_paragraph: Experts say immersion in cold water before an ambulance arrives can greatly increase the chances of heat stroke survival and reduce the risk of long-term complications.

title: The Federal Reserve faces a critical decision on interest rates
first_paragraph: Policymakers at the Federal Reserve are meeting to discuss interest rates Wednesday. They're expected to hold rates steady, but there's a chance they could raise rates to combat stubborn inflation.

title: To win over working-class voters, Democrats need to stop talking about democracy
first_paragraph: Working-class voters have moved away from the Democratic Party. Winning them back is key to the party's future, a new reports shows. But first, the messaging has to change.

title: More Americans are going bankrupt. What does that mean?
first_paragraph: The bankruptcy rate has risen about 48% between 2022 and 2025, although it's still below pre-pandemic levels.

title: Anthony Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment in Rand Paul Senate hearing
first_paragraph: At a Senate hearing Wednesday, Anthony Fauci is likely to face questions from Sen. Rand Paul related to the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic. Here's what you need to know

title: France evacuates thousands as fires displace a third of a million in southwest Europe
first_paragraph: French authorities ordered 4,000 more people evacuated from tourist sites along its Atlantic coast, widening what may be France's largest peacetime evacuation.

title: Death toll rises to 18 as rescuers comb through quake rubble in southwestern Japan
first_paragraph: Soldiers and emergency workers combed through a badly damaged shopping mall and collapsed houses looking for trapped survivors Wednesday after a powerful earthquake that killed at least 18 people, including a foreigner, in southwestern Japan.

title: As Spain battles wildfires, its politicians battle over climate change's role
first_paragraph: Crews are still battling wildfires that broke out last week and have burned nearly 200,000 acres across Spain. The country is bracing for another round of extreme heat, with temperatures expected to top 100 degrees Fahrenheit starting Wednesday.

title: Keiko Fujimori is inaugurated as Peru's president following a narrow election victory
first_paragraph: The 51-year-old daughter of the late former President Alberto Fujimori, Peru's new conservative leader has pledged to fight crime with an "iron fist."

title: Trump meets Ukrainian, Israeli leaders as they pay respects to Lindsey Graham
first_paragraph: President Trump holds talks with Ukrainian and Israeli leaders on the sidelines of Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral.

title: Ukraine negotiator: 'We have the upper hand'
first_paragraph: In an interview with NPR, one of Ukraine's top negotiators Sergiy Kyslytsya explains why Kyiv believes it now has the leverage to force Russia into serious negotiations.

title: Photos: Spain and France battle record wildfires
first_paragraph: Hundreds of thousands of people have been forced from their homes as powerful wildfires sweep across Spain and France, revealing the growing scale of a climate crisis already reshaping the continent.

title: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says he had a 'good meeting' with Trump in Washington
first_paragraph: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he had a "good meeting" with President Donald Trump Tuesday, as the country seeks to make more weapons in its fight against Russia.

title: Did Zelenskyy get what he needed from his D.C. visit? Former ambassador weighs in
first_paragraph: NPR's Leila Fadel asks former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine William Taylor about what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy obtained from his visit to Washington.

title: Senate confirms Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence
first_paragraph: The Senate confirmed Jay Clayton to oversee the intelligence community, despite Democrats' concerns that he could politicize intelligence at President Trump's direction.

title: Trump and Netanyahu meet in D.C. amid tensions over Iran war
first_paragraph: President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's latest meeting comes as the U.S. has paused strikes in Iran as the two sides negotiate.

title: Former peace negotiator shares takeaways from Trump's meeting with Netanyahu
first_paragraph: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former peace negotiator and advisor to the Israeli government Daniel Levy about takeaways from President Trump's meeting with Israel's prime minister.

title: Haitian TPS holders in South Florida brace for end of their legal status
first_paragraph: Temporary protected status was given to Haitians after the 2010 quake because Haiti was deemed too dangerous for a safe return. In June, the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to end TPS.

title: Democrats are focused on affordability. Some say they should focus on democracy too
first_paragraph: Democratic candidates have focused on affordability. But some party leaders say they also need to talk about democracy, especially if President Trump continues making unfounded claims about election fraud.

title: FIFA has a new plan to raise billions of dollars: Selling stakes in the World Cup
first_paragraph: FIFA has a complex plan to sell chunks of its commercial rights to the World Cup to minority investors, including a firm run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Jared Kushner.

title: As many are priced out of buying, the renter-owner wealth gap is wider than ever
first_paragraph: Record high housing costs have pushed the wealth gap between renters and owners wider than ever. It's been a boon for owners even as many others are priced out.

title: AI tokens could become the kilowatt-hour of the AI age
first_paragraph: AI companies use tokens to track usage and bill customers. Now economists are using them to track the spread of AI through the economy.

title: Yes, it's possible to save money while paying off credit card debt. Here's how
first_paragraph: In fact, experts recommend it because it can keep you off the hamster wheel of debt. Here's how to find the money in your budget to put toward savings and credit card payments.

title: Kalshi attacks a Wisconsin law banning election bets as 'voter suppression'
first_paragraph: The spat between the leading prediction market company and a key battleground state could be a glimpse into the next major fight between states and the fast-growing industry.

title: Toy company CEO shares how Trump's new round of tariffs could affect business
first_paragraph: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Jay Foreman of toy importer Basic Fun! about President Trump's latest round of tariffs. The company has paid millions of dollars in import duties under Trump.

title: Oil prices are climbing again. Here's why this time could be different
first_paragraph: Oil prices surpassed $100 a barrel last week. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Bob McNally, founder of the research firm Rapidan Energy Group, about how the Iran war is disrupting oil supplies.

title: Rage-giving, innovation and cuts: How public media has survived without federal funds
first_paragraph: A year after President Trump signed a law ending six decades of federal funding of public media, it's a time of reinvention, innovation and clear anxiety at public tv and radio stations nationwide.

title: AI executive calls OpenAI hacking event a wake-up call for the industry
first_paragraph: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Thomas Wolf, co-founder and chief science officer for Hugging Face, an AI company, discusses the recent hacking incident involving ChatGPT.

title: Allegations of AI distillation spark debate about IP theft. But is it illegal?
first_paragraph: Distillation lets AI companies train new models using existing ones. The White House says Chinese firms are using it to gain an edge, raising questions about competition and intellectual property.

title: Authors have mixed feelings about the $1.5B Anthropic copyright infringement ruling
first_paragraph: Some say the $3,100 per title payout is small compensation for what they view as big, ongoing threats from the makers of generative AI models.

title: Sony says it will stop producing physical discs for PlayStation games
first_paragraph: Sony's Playstation games once ran solely on discs. But with advances in technology, physical discs are unnecessary, and the company will soon stop making them.

title: A town renamed its festival 'AI Love Irondale Day.' Then came the comments
first_paragraph: The online outcry over the renaming of a summer festival illustrates the unease over the data center boom in the South.

title: OpenAI says AI models hacked into another AI company without being instructed
first_paragraph: NPR's A Martinez asks Nate Soares of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute how two experimental OpenAI models hacked their way onto the internet and into another AI company, without instruction.

title: Federal funds can't be spent on giving drug users test strips, raising overdose fears
first_paragraph: Test strips can identify dangerous hidden additives in street drugs and help prevent overdoses. But the Trump administration says federal funds can't be used to provide the strips to drug users.

title: Cuts to funds and staffing have slowed the response to the cyclospora outbreak
first_paragraph: Recent cuts, especially to state and local health departments, are slowing and muddling the response to what's already a record year of outbreaks for diarrhea-causing cyclospora.

title: Amid U.S. funding cuts, the International AIDS Conference faces an uncertain future
first_paragraph: Dr. Kenneth Ngure, president-elect of the International AIDS Society, says, "We have had very good scientific advances ... yet the funding cuts have also taken us back."

title: Rand Paul releases Anthony Fauci's pandemic-era diary notes. Here's what they tell us
first_paragraph: Sen. Rand Paul has released a tranche of Dr. Anthony Fauci's diary entries from the COVID-19 pandemic. Fauci is set to appear before a Senate committee Wednesday on the origins of the coronavirus.

title: Pakistan study suggests microbiome may influence preterm birth
first_paragraph: A Pakistan study finds one bacteria in pregnant women's colons can indicate her likelihood of reaching full term or having a premature baby.

title: Baltimore will turn 911 into more than just an emergency number
first_paragraph: Baltimore is rethinking what it means to call 911, and who responds. Callers who don't need police will get help finding social services and healthcare before they actually fall into crisis.

title: More than 2,000 measles cases reported in the U.S. so far, outpacing 2025's total
first_paragraph: NPR's A Martinez asks Dr. Jennifer Nuzzo of Brown University why there have been more measles cases this year so far than in all of last year, and what can be done to stop the resurgence.

title: How cuts to federal agencies led to the current cyclosporiasis outbreak
first_paragraph: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks with NBC health and medical news reporter Erika Edwards about the Trump Administration's cuts to federal agencies affects food safety measures.

title: ADHD looks different in women and poses unique health risks
first_paragraph: For decades, ADHD was viewed as a childhood condition that mostly affected boys. Researchers now know ADHD manifests differently in girls, but many still go undiagnosed until adulthood.

title: How researchers discovered a new monkey species deep in the rainforest
first_paragraph: In the jungle of the Democratic Republic of Congo, a team of researchers discover a new species of monkey, and form a deep friendship along the way.

title: France continues to fight devastating wildfires, while progress is made in Spain
first_paragraph: In southern France, a wildfire in the region of Gironde is still active, while two major fires in central Spain are finally coming under control, ahead of the fourth heat wave of the summer.

title: Climate change is now threatening a pillar of childhood: summer break
first_paragraph: When summer rolls around, many parents scramble to sign up their young kids for outdoor activities. But what do you do when extreme heat and wildfire smoke increasingly make the outdoors dangerous?

title: Trump officials herald a 'golden age' of science. Critics say it's a distraction
first_paragraph: White House officials say they are ushering in a new "golden age" of science, with changes to grantmaking and priorities like AI and quantum computing. Democrats say it masks damage to U.S. science.

title: Video: Scientists watch orcas ram a sunfish so hard it explodes
first_paragraph: Marine biologists off of Baja California recorded one orca teeing up another to smash a sunfish into pieces. Scientists say there could be a reason for this behavior — or it could be just for entertainment.

title: Egyptian warrior princesses, ancient avocados, and more science news
first_paragraph: Hannah Chin and Nate Rott of NPR's Short Wave podcast talk about the building blocks of birdsong, the evolutionary history of avocados and Egyptian warrior princesses.

title: Trump cuts target federal advisory boards. What does it mean for agencies like NASA?
first_paragraph: The Trump administration has terminated or suspended more than 100 federal advisory committees. Former members say agencies like NASA now have less accountability to stakeholders and the public.

title: 50 years after landmark laws, some U.S. rivers are recovering but threats remain
first_paragraph: Half a century ago, a series of landmark federal laws started reining in water pollution. As a result, some rivers across the country are bouncing back to life, but threats to clean rivers remain.

title: Kill your lawn, plant native flowers
first_paragraph: Traditional lawns may be green, but that doesn't mean they're good for the environment. The team at NPR's Life Kit podcast report on one lawn alternative that's gaining popularity.

title: A strange transmissible cancer is spreading through the catfish in this lake
first_paragraph: For more than a decade, there's been something fishy going on in a lake that straddles Vermont and the province of Quebec. It involves cancer, a kind of catfish, and — possibly — clues about how tumors metastasize.

title: An Israeli paraglider tries to save migrating swifts that nest in the Western Wall
first_paragraph: Swifts have nested in Jerusalem's Western Wall since biblical times. Now one Israeli paraglider is trying to save them.

title: What we can learn from the unique smell of wildfire smoke
first_paragraph: NPR's Adrian Ma speaks with Derek Mallia, professor University of Utah's Department of Atmospheric Sciences, about why wildfire smoke in the northeast has a distinctive smell.

title: Dangerous wildfire smoke continues to blanket parts of the U.S.
first_paragraph: Orange skies and heavy smoke covered large parts of the U.S. on Thursday as Canada and Minnesota grapple with wildfires. Hazardous air quality is expected to continue.

title: Fear and hope in Utah in the shadow of America's largest wildfire
first_paragraph: People in Monticello, Utah have been tense and preparing to evacuate since shortly after the Babylon fire started June 26th

title: We hear from the class of 2026 on how post-grad life is going
first_paragraph: Graduates in the class of 2026 are navigating an unusually choppy labor market. We talked to three fresh grads about their post-grad experience so far.

title: Meet the robots programmed by kids to speak their Indigenous languages
first_paragraph: Many Native American languages are endangered. With the help of his mentor, a 12-year-old in Michigan hopes to help preserve his language through robotics.

title: How to keep an ancient text interesting to students? Make it a summer blockbuster
first_paragraph: English teachers are excited to have a new adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey to use to get students excited about the epic poem.

title: India's Gen Z 'Cockroach People's Party' started as satire but is serious about change
first_paragraph: They call themselves the "cockroaches" and they're on the march — demanding action against corruption, amid a shortage of opportunities for young people in India.

title: How the Trump administration's new rules could affect international students
first_paragraph: International students could once stay as long as they needed to complete their college degrees, but that's changing, and the restrictions could cut into college budgets.

title: How do young people feel about AI? 7 teens weigh in
first_paragraph: What's it like to grow up and learn in the age of AI? NPR put that question to seven teenagers across the country.

title: No internet, no screen time? FCC weighs cutting subsidy that lowers school internet bills
first_paragraph: Many schools rely on consumer fees funneled through the federal government to cut internet costs. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr called for ending this program before Donald Trump tapped him for the job.

title: Some Republican states push for new college accreditation agency
first_paragraph: Some Republican states are starting a new college accreditation agency to increase what they call "intellectual diversity".

title: In private call, Education Dept. tried, but failed, to reassure disability advocates
first_paragraph: The disability community has long worried about what would happen if special education oversight moved from the Education Department to another agency. Now, those moves are becoming more real.

title: Should you sign your kids up for Trump Accounts? Four things to consider
first_paragraph: Families can still benefit even if their children aren't eligible for the free $1,000 contribution from the federal government.
